_comment: Role -> model seat. Every seat has a fallback on a DIFFERENT family. Model changes happen only through `pipeline trial` (staged head-to-head with a rubric); vendor benchmarks nominate, never decide. `pipeline render-agents` regenerates the devpass-code agent files from this registry and CI diffs them (drift guard).

interactive.purpose: The one agent the operator talks to. Routes every ask into quick or plan; never does the work itself.

history.why: DECISION interactive-fallback: operator chose glm-5.3 as the manual standard-tier fallback for the interactive seat when the premium allowance is hit; to be revisited by trial-report interactive

DECISION no-premium-seats: the registry never seats a premium model in any field, including interactive; glm-5.3 (the operator's stated preference) becomes the interim primary until trial-report interactive names the measured best standard-tier arm.

implementer.purpose: Code changes with tests, exact ceremony (commit subject, verification grep).

history.why: DECISION interim-standard-seats (2026-09-04): premium allowance 402s recur; working seats moved to standard-tier so plan 004 can finish; trials revisit.

DECISION cost-swap implementer->terra (2026-09-07, operator-approved): measured journal spend showed claude-sonnet-5 at 58% of all estate cost ($127.71 of $221.12 across 328 dispatches), with 34 of its 75 implementer dispatches not landing ok (the timeout class). gpt-5.6-terra@high is published-cheaper by 4.1x ($0.81 vs $3.31/task blended; $1.75/$7.00 vs $2.00/$10.00 per M in/out, gateway pricing) with comparable-or-better evidence: AA Intelligence 47 vs 45, LiveBench code_completion 80.4 vs 78.3, typescript 46.7 vs 50.0 (sonnet slightly ahead), code_generation 76.1 vs 83.1 (sonnet's edge, from-scratch work; the implementer role here is mostly completing/fixing code). Sources: artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models and livebench.ai/table_2026_06_25.csv, both retrieved 2026-09-05, in docs/model-selection/SEAT-EVIDENCE.md. Same swap applied to frontend-worker (same seat, zero dispatches so far, identical criteria). Sonnet-5 remains seated as interactive-fallback and reviewer fallbacks; the from-scratch codegen edge is noted and re-checkable via pipeline trial if implementer quality regresses.

fast-worker.purpose: Small, well-specified, cheap: a fetch, a one-line fix, a file rename.

history.why: DECISION published-benchmarks (2026-09-05): operator directed seat changes to follow published benchmarks, not token trials. No model tokens spent.

history.why: DECISION fallback-sweep (2026-09-06, completed by the interactor after two worker timeouts left the analysis unfinished): criterion = same as the primary's. For researcher/document-writer (reading/digesting, prose) the published numbers rank glm-5.3 above claude-sonnet-5 on every axis of the role's criterion: LiveBench summarize 74.55 vs 71.22, AA intelligence 49 vs 45, TTFT 2.0s vs 2.9s (sources: artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models, livebench.ai/table_2026_06_25.csv, both retrieved 2026-09-05, in docs/model-selection/SEAT-EVIDENCE.md). kimi-k3's AA 50 is beaten here by its LB summarize 69.35 (below sonnet's 71.22) and TTFT 28.5s. Interactive KEEPS claude-sonnet-5: conversational TTFT 2.9s beats kimi-k3's 28.5s; glm-5.3 is unusable as its own fallback (same model as the primary). No other seat's fallback changed: each current one already wins its role's criterion (implementer gpt-5.6-luna on code speed/cost, reviewers deepseek-v4-pro/gpt-5.3-codex/gemini-3.8-flash on intelligence+TTFT).
